title: Judge the artifact, not the writer
statement: Check every generated item independently, since a writer's score on teaching questions, its grasp of a pedagogy and its own report of compliance are no evidence of what it makes.
example: A model that scored 96.52% on a pedagogy benchmark was published with the caution that this is not evidence of effective tutoring.
detail: The reading project's comprehension doctrine deliberately rejects two kinds of evidence about generated lessons: pedagogy-benchmark scores, which measure knowing that rather than generating content that embodies it, and a model's unaudited assessment of its own content (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0121-teaching-comprehension-insights-brainlift.qmd`). Its experiment intake lets a model assist extraction but never certify its own atom, and counts a model's self-reported compliance as no evidence (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0131-pedagogy-decision-bank-experiment-intake.qmd`); its feedback routing says no lane can self-certify the whole course (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0164-g3-v2-feedback-agent-routing.qmd`). A published model tuned for pedagogy reached 96.52% on a pedagogical-knowledge benchmark, and the paper itself says such performance is not evidence of effective classroom tutoring (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0124-eduqwen-pedagogical-llm-paper.qmd`). The independent check should come from a different model family than the writer.
against: The doctrine's 'empirically worthless' points to a leak rate in raw generated items, not to a study of self-assessment (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0121-teaching-comprehension-insights-brainlift.qmd`). the same paper reports that its training moved the model toward guided-learning responses rather than giving answers, a project plan proposes training a model on its own teaching principles, and whether that reaches generated material was left as an experiment. This is the project's own synthesis, which marks itself as paraphrase-level and not quote-checked, so the 78% and 79% are summaries of its measurements, not the measurements themselves (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/skills/reading-science/applied/teaching-comprehension-insights-brainlift.qmd`). judging with three model families was proposed but not approved, and no evidence was presented that it reduces evaluator flakiness (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0127-incept-service-coe-catchup-2026-07-14.qmd`, lines 85-86).

evidence.quote: A model may assist extraction but may not certify its own atom.
Model self-reported compliance is not evidence; measure agreement before adjudication.
unaudited LLM self-assessment of its own content (empirically worthless — see DOK1-11)
pedagogy-benchmark scores as evidence of teaching ability (measures knowing-that, not generating-aligned)
no lane can self-certify the whole course.
strong benchmark performance on pedagogical knowledge questions does not itself constitute evidence of effective classroom tutoring
reaches 96.52% on the Cross-Domain Pedagogical Knowledge (CDPK) benchmark
Knowing-that (answering pedagogy questions) and generating-aligned (producing content that embodies the pedagogy) are different capabilities
the gap is invisible to benchmarks and only measurable at the artifact level
a dose that "knew" gradual release still leaked its item's answer
RL shifted behavior "toward guided-learning-like response patterns… rather than direct answer provision"
training an LLM specifically on the team's pedagogical principles rather than only using it to generate content
left downstream transfer as an experiment

Generation systematically betrays declared pedagogy — \~78% of raw generated reading items were answerable without the passage, correct answers sat at position A 79% of the time, and a dose that "knew" gradual release still leaked its item's answer — and design-time contracts alone demonstrably failed to prevent any of it.

Knowing-that (answering pedagogy questions) and generating-aligned (producing content that embodies the pedagogy) are different capabilities; the gap is invisible to benchmarks and only measurable at the artifact level.
REJECTS pedagogy-benchmark scores as teaching evidence.
filed with its own caveat that benchmark PCK ≠ teaching ability
Our own synthesis (paraphrase-level cites), NOT external evidence — not quote-gated.

Knowing-that (answering pedagogy questions) and generating-aligned (producing content that embodies the pedagogy) are different capabilities; the gap must be measured at the artifact level rather than inferred from benchmark scores.
knowing-that != generating-aligned (kb-0121 SPOV2, kb-0124 EduQwen authors' own limitation)
a generator can "know" gradual release and still emit answer-reveals.
The questions were good because the generator was not trusted.
- do not trust LLM self-report; - only gate outputs and read-back artifacts count; - a lane cannot certify its own items;
3. Use a different family for the gate than for the author. Never same-family certify.
The binding gate must stay **cross-family** (solver family != generator family); IB self-certification is not anti-leak evidence.
A model's pedagogical knowledge does not survive the trip into its generated content.
the gap must be measured at the artifact level rather than inferred from benchmark scores.
Does training on pedagogical principles produce a model that GENERATES aligned lessons -- not merely one that answers pedagogy questions?
knowing pedagogy does not prove generated content embodies it. This is why JSON validity and question accuracy cannot be the headline.
Model self-reported compliance is not evidence; measure agreement before adjudication.
- treating "model says it is fixed" as evidence.
beats were paraphrased instead of copied verbatim from the catalog, and the self-red-team log had **falsely claimed "verbatim."**
